name.text: Determining tangent using the unit circle

questiontext.text:
The angle \(\theta={@theta@}^\circ\) is measured in standard position. Use the unit circle to determine the exact value of \(\tan\theta\).

Recall that \(\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}.\)

Give your answer in exact form. Do not use a decimal approximation.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

Step 1: Identify the angle and reference angle

The given angle is \(\theta={@theta@}^\circ\), and its reference angle is \({@ref_angle@}^\circ\).

The reference angle helps us determine the exact magnitudes of the sine and cosine values.

Step 2: Recall the tangent formula

Tangent is the ratio of sine to cosine:

\(\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}.\)

Step 3: Determine sine and cosine

Using the coordinates of the corresponding point on the unit circle, we obtain

\[ \sin\theta={@sin_theta@} \]

and

\(\cos\theta={@cos_theta@}.\)

Step 4: Calculate tangent

Substitute these values into the tangent formula:

\(\tan\theta=\frac{{@sin_theta@}}{{@cos_theta@}}.\)

Simplifying gives

\(\tan\theta={@tan_theta@}.\)

Final answer

\(\tan({@theta@}^\circ)={@tan_theta@}.\)
